source.author: verg
source.text: Ergo instauramus Polydoro funus, et ingens aggeritur tumulo tellus; stant Manibus arae, caeruleis maestae vittis atraque cupresso, et circum Iliades crinem de more solutae; inferimus tepido spumantia cymbia lacte sanguinis et sacri pateras, animamque sepulchro condimus, et magna supremum voce ciemus.
source.text_original: Ergo instauramus Polydoro funus, et ingens / aggeritur tumulo tellus; stant Manibus arae, / caeruleis maestae vittis atraque cupresso, / et circum Iliades crinem de more solutae; / inferimus tepido spumantia cymbia lacte / sanguinis et sacri pateras, animamque sepulchro / condimus, et magna supremum voce ciemus.
source.text_english: So we renew the funeral rites for Polydorus, and a great mound of earth is heaped over his tomb; altars stand for his Shades, sorrowful with dark ribbons and black cypress, and around them are the Trojan women, their hair loosened as the custom is; we pour into the grave foaming bowls of warm milk and cups of sacred blood, and we lay his spirit in the tomb, and with a loud voice we call him for the last time.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: veteris sub nocte cupressi sordidus et multa pallens ferrugine taurus stabat adhuc, cui caeruleae per cornua vittae et taxi frons hirta comis; ipse aeger anhelans impatiensque loci visaque exterritus umbra.
reuse.text_original: veteris sub nocte cupressi / sordidus et multa pallens ferrugine taurus / stabat adhuc, cui caeruleae per cornua vittae / et taxi frons hirta comis; ipse aeger anhelans / impatiensque loci visaque exterritus umbra.
reuse.text_english: Beneath the darkness of an ancient cypress stood a bull, dirty and pale with much rust-colored stain still upon it; blue ribbons ran over its horns, and its brow was bristling with yew-like hairs. He himself was sick, panting, and impatient of the place, terrified by the sight even of a shadow.
